quote: I’ve learned to live simply, wisely, / To look at the sky and pray to God, / And to take long walks before evening / To wear out this useless anxiety.
source: Anna Akhmatova, ‘I’ve learned to live simply, wisely’ (1912), Rosary, lines 1 to 4 (trans. Judith Hemschemeyer, 1990)

evidence.where: Poetry Chaikhana reprint crediting The Complete Poems of Anna Akhmatova, ed. Roberta Reeder, trans. Judith Hemschemeyer; the stanza agrees with other reprints of Hemschemeyer; the Zephyr volume itself was not opened, so no page is cited
evidence.edition: The Complete Poems of Anna Akhmatova, trans. Judith Hemschemeyer, ed. Roberta Reeder (Somerville, MA: Zephyr Press, 1990), Rosary (Chetki, 1914) section
evidence.locator: opening stanza, lines 1 to 4, of ‘Ya nauchilas prosto, mudro zhit’, written 1912, collected in Rosary (1914)

reason: The stanza is the poem’s opening in Hemschemeyer’s wording and lineation, as reprinted with credit to the Zephyr Complete Poems; the poem is of 1912 and belongs to Rosary (1914). Confidence is medium because the check is against credited reprints, not the printed page. The translation is in copyright, which the editor should weigh. Not shipped, Akhmatova unused, not banned.
